Nami: Make Vayne shutdown at 4% battery charge Currently, Vayne and all other Nami's shutdown when battery charge (=soc) goes below 3%. This patch makes Vayne set shutdown charge level to 4% to match Powerd's threshold. When system is running or in suspend, Vayne behaves as follows: 1. Powerd shuts down system when soc < 4. (EC also catches soc < 4 but takes no action.) If Powerd fails to shut down system or system is in suspend, EC forces system to shut down. 2. System shuts down. 3. charger task cuts off battery. When system is off or in suspend, EC cuts off battery in 30 secs after soc <= 4%. Signed-off-by: Daisuke Nojiri <dnojiri@chromium.org> BUG=b/123727148 BRANCH=nami TEST=Verify Vayne cuts off battery when soc <= 4% in s0 and s5. u2fd: Support software keys for U2F_REGISTER attestation. A portion of a valid U2F_REGISTER response must be signed by an attestation key, and the response must also include an X509 certificate for that attestation key. Currently cr50 provides this functionality, however for non-G2F authentication this is not necessary, and the attestation can be done purely in software. This change adds support to u2fd for software-based attestation. vboot/screens: Get rid of video console, use HWID font for everything This patch changes VbExDisplayDebugInfo() to use the HWID font (which now includes all printable characters) and overall make it a little prettier. This allows us to completely eliminate the dependency on the libpayload video console and the corebootfb framebuffer driver for normal images. corebootfb and cbgfx have always been sort of parallel implementations for roughly the same stuff that both write to the framebuffer directly, so it's cleaner to only use one of them for everything. Fastboot, netboot and CLI images continue to use the video console for specific developer use cases (which is probably fine), but production images no longer pull any of it in (which saves about 3KB/3% of the compressed payload binary on my Kevin). BRANCH=None BUG=None TEST=Played around with TAB output on Kevin, both with and without bitmaps in CBFS, configured for both normal and detachable UI. login: Use Minijail to launch Chrome. session_manager had a lot of bespoke process-launching logic for starting Chrome. Replace this with a straightforward Minijail invocation that removes a lot of duplicate code. Moreover, this will allow adding further sandboxing very easily. This CL does not change current sandboxing. Namely, we still: * Switch to user/group 'chronos' (1000), and inherit 'chronos' groups. * Close all fd's except for stdin/stdout/stderr. * For guest mode sessions, enter a new mount namespace. This CL is a net decrease of about 50 lines of code. Also re-add 'subprocess_test.cc' to the list of test targets which might have been dropped in the GN conversion. BUG=chromium:931255 TEST=New unit tests. TEST=Build and deploy to grunt, Guest mode works. usb_chg: Add USB_CHG events for data role set and CC open The pi3usb9201 bc1.2 chip has both client and host mode support. Other bc1.2 detection chips support client mode and are triggered by VBUS detection events. To have better control of the pi3usb9201 and to prevent d+/d- data interruption, it's preferable to trigger bc1.2 mode on data role updates as the data role setting is what's most relevant to legacy bc1.2 modes. This CL adds 3 new USB_CHG events that can be set in the USB PD protocol layer when the data role is being set to sink or source and when a detach event occurs. BUG=b:124612788 BRANCH=none TEST=Tested both external chargers, adapters, and charge through hubs. Verfied that bc1.2 detection is triggered as expected when chargers are connected and verified that when the type C port is in source mode, then the pi3usb9201 is in host CDP mode.
